title: V Modern Italian May Join The Lakefront at Scottsdale - WhatNow

title: A24 Developing SCP Foundation Film, Adapting Hit Internet Property for 'V/H/S' Franchise Expansion - TheWrap
content: The project comes as a joint production with Spooky Pictures and Image Nation Studios The hit internet horror universe SCP Foundation is coming to the big screen as a new extension of the “V/H/S” horror franchise. A24, Spooky Pictures and Image Nation Studios are teaming up on a feature-length film based on the SCP Foundation, the internet-born, fan-created horror and science-fiction property. The film is set for theatrical release in 2027, with A24 holding worldwide rights. It marks the first feature-length film based on the SCP Foundation, a collaborative mythology that originated online in 2008 and has since been expanded by thousands of contributors around the world. The universe encompasses stories involving anomalous objects, entities and phenomena and has inspired games, short films and web series. A24 will co-produce the film with Roy Lee and Steven Schneider for Spooky Pictures, alongside Josh Goldbloom and Michael Schreiber. Goldbloom has produced several “V/H/S” films, including “V/H/S/94,” “V/H/S/99” and “V/H/S/Halloween.” Schreiber also worked on “V/H/S/94” and “V/H/S/Beyond.” Image Nation Studios CEO Ben Ross and Spooky Pictures’ Rami Yasin and Jakob Pollack will executive produce alongside Brad Miska. “Internet lore is quickly rising as a compelling source of new stories for the horror genre, bringing with it built-in, highly devoted audiences,” Image Nation Studios’ CEO Ben Ross and Spooky Pictures co-founders Roy Lee and Steven Schneider said in a joint statement. “As fans increasingly seek out fresh scares, we’re focused on tapping into the most compelling online worlds in which talent already live, such as the vast SCP universe, and helping them make the leap to the big screen.” The statement continues: “With A24’s expertise in nurturing and elevating internet-born phenomena like ‘Backrooms’ into major theatrical success, they’re the ideal partner for ‘V/H/S: SCP’ and we can’t wait to expand the franchise with new, spine-chilling stories together.” The announcement follows the companies’ acquisition of rights to the “V/H/S” found-footage anthology franchise earlier this year. The SCP Foundation film will be the next installment in the series, following “V/H/S/Mixtape,” a music-themed anthology that is set to premiere on Shudder in October. A24’s “Backrooms” has grossed $394 million worldwide. The film marked the feature debut of Kane Parsons and was based on his viral internet shorts about the liminal spaces of the Backrooms.

title: NetChoice v. Illinois - NetChoice
content:
Case Status: Complaints filed in the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois 
Latest Update: September 11, 2026
Attorneys: Illinois’ new Social Media User Tax and Digital Ad Tax firmly cement the state’s position as anti-speech, anti-innovation, and anti-internet freedom. These taxes stand in direct opposition to federal law, violate the First Amendment, and raise a host of other constitutional problems. NetChoice is suing to prevent Illinois from demoting online speech to second-class status. NetChoice sued on September 11, 2026, to ensure protected online content is able to flourish without unconstitutional burdens. Read the complaint against the Social Media User Tax here, and read the complaint against the Digital Ad Tax here. The Supreme Court has made it clear that the First Amendment does not “go on leave” when social media is involved. The Social Media User Tax targets media companies for disfavored tax treatment based on audience size. In Minneapolis Star & Tribune Co. v. Minnesota Commissioner of Revenue, the Supreme Court struck down a similar tax on paper and ink that applied only after publishers exceeded $100,000 in expenditures. The Court found that exempting smaller publishers while discriminating based on circulation size violated the First Amendment. By exempting online services with fewer than 100,000 users while penalizing those with larger audiences, the tax creates a “disfavored” category of media companies based purely on their reach. Taxing a service based on its “active users” is a direct tax on the medium of speech and the community connection that these services facilitate. That discrimination violates the First Amendment. Illinois’ Social Media User Tax follows the same blueprint NetChoice is already challenging in NetChoice v. Chicago, a pending suit over the city’s own per-user Social Media Amusement Tax. Furthermore, under the Permanent Internet Tax Freedom Act (PITFA), Congress explicitly prohibited states from imposing “discriminatory taxes on electronic commerce.” Both the Social Media User Tax and the Digital Ad Tax are in direct violation of PITFA. Both taxes apply exclusively to online services while leaving comparable offline counterparts — social clubs, community centers, professional associations, and traditional advertising — untouched. This is precisely the sort of digital-only taxation Congress intended to preempt, and similar laws, including Maryland’s Digital Advertising Tax, have already been struck down by courts on comparable grounds. Both taxes hurt Illinoisans and their businesses. The Digital Ad Tax hurts small businesses, including restaurants, auto dealers, and community organizations, by increasing costs or limiting access to vital online marketing and communication tools relied on by local small businesses to compete against their much larger competitors. Additionally, because the Social Media User Tax is a flat fee untethered to a company’s actual revenue or profit in Illinois, some services may choose to limit or exit the Illinois market altogether — cutting residents off from vital communication, educational, and community-organizing tools they rely on daily. NetChoice’s Complaint against the Social Media User Tax, filed on September 11, 2026, in the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois. NetChoice’s Complaint against the Digital Ad Tax, filed on September 11, 2026, in the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois.

title: Biofer S.P.A. v. Vifor (International) AG (Fed Cir. 2026) - JD Supra
content:
Measurement of the hydrogen ion concentration in an aqueous solution is represented (on a logarithmic scale) as the pH, wherein water under ambient conditions (a temperature of 25°C) has a neutral pH of 7 and the solution becomes more acidic as the pH value trends towards 1 and more basic as it trends towards 14. Characterizing such solutions as elements of patent claims has a long judicial history (being critical in the seminal case on the doctrine of equivalents, Warner-Jenkinson Co., Inc. v. Hilton David Chemical Co.) and the property was recently the basis of the Federal Circuit’s decision in Biofer S.P.A. v. Vifor (International) AG (non-precedential). The case arose in patent infringement litigation wherein Biofer filed suit asserting U.S. Patent No. 8,759,320, directed to trivalent iron complexes with various forms of sugars (specifically dextrins and dextrans). Claim 1 was set forth in the opinion as being representative: 1. A process for the preparation of an activated sugar comprising the step of reacting a sugar having an aldehyde end group with bromine in a solution at a pH between 7.0 and 9.0 with the specific oxidation of the end aldehyde, wherein i) said sugar is selected from the group consisting of dextrins and dextrans and wherein ii) said bromine is produced in situ through the addition of a hypochlorite and an alkaline or earth alkaline metal bromide to said solution, said hypochlorite being added in stoichiometric quantities with respect to the aldehyde end groups, wherein said hypochlorite is added instant by instant, such that an excess of hypochlorite in solution is never present. The invention provided an improvement on prior art processes for producing complexes for treating iron deficiencies that accommodate required “fundamental characteristics, such as physical and chemical stability, low toxicity, and good bioavailability” necessary for therapeutic use. Of the four synthetic steps required in the process, the claims (and appeal) were directed to activating the sugar for producing an iron complex. This activation step was illustrated in the diagram. which was accomplished by performing the claimed oxidation reaction with bromine in solution. The opinion also explains that specific aldehyde moieties in dextrins and dextrans are advantageous (i.e., at the ends of the sugar polymer) because permitting the reaction to proceed elsewhere in the sugar molecule was associated with undesirable instabilities. In practice, correct oxidation required a solution pH “in the range between 5.0 and 12.0, preferably, between 7.0 and 9.0.” The District Court construed the pH limitation and practice of the synthetic methods falling within the scope of claim 1 to mean that the pH range of 7.0 to 9.0 must be maintained throughout the process, based on the intrinsic evidence and in particular the disclosure in the specification (see below). Because discovery revealed that Vifor’s process only maintained a pH within the construed range “approximately 90% of the time,” Biofer stipulated that the accused process did not infringe (while informing the District Court of its intention to appeal). In that appeal the Federal Circuit affirmed, in an opinion by Judge Reyna joined by Judges Linn and Dyk. Beginning with the claim language, the opinion asserts that the plain meaning of the phrase “at a pH between 7.0 and 9.0” modifies “the step of reacting a sugar” and that this “step” refers to “the entire oxidation step” of the disclosed synthetic process. The disclosure of the specification is consistent with this interpretation, in the panel’s view, wherein it recited that “to avoid undesirable depolymerization, ‘it is important to maintain the reaction pH in the range between 5.0 and 12.0, preferably, between 7.0 and 9.0′” (albeit this phrase could just as easily be reasonably construed to mean that the reaction be maintained in the range of pH 5.0 to 12.0). Elsewhere in the specification, however, the “maintain” limitation is restricted to a pH range of 7.0 to 9.0, supporting the District Court’s construction, further supported by the three examples expressly directed to performance of the oxidation step being achieved between pH 7.0 and 9.0. The Federal Circuit relied upon GPNE Corp. v. Apple Inc., 830 F.3d 1365, 1370 (Fed. Cir. 2016) (quoting VirnetX, Inc. v. Cisco Sys., Inc., 767 F.3d 1308, 1318 (Fed. Cir. 2014)), for the principle that when a patent “‘repeatedly and consistently’ characterizes a claim term in a particular way” that is the proper way the term should be construed. Finally, the prosecution history was consistent with this conclusion, wherein Biofer had submitted an expert declaration attesting that performing the oxidation reaction between pH 7.8 and 8.2 was “highly selective without increasing depolymerization,” while performing the reaction between 9.8 and 10.2 “led to a depolymerizing attack on the sugar.” Biofer argued that the District Court’s construction improperly relied upon a preferred embodiment (pH 7.0 to 9.0) instead of construing the pH range throughout it entire scope (pH 5.0 to 12.0). The panel acknowledged the broader pH range, but the claim having only recited the narrower pH 7.0 to 9.0 range was dispositive for the Court. Further (oral) argument that the process could be construed to permit the pH to encounter “brief excursions” outside the narrower range but within the broader range was precluded by Biofer’s failure to raise this argument below according to the opinion, citing Conoco, Inc. v. Energy & Env’t Int’l, L.C., 460 F.3d 1349, 1358–59 (Fed. Cir. 2006) (it not helping Biofer’s argument that it had raised what appeared to the panel to be an opposite argument before the District Court). Biofer S.P.A. v. Vifor (International) AG (Fed Cir. 2026)

title: Hero GTA V Modder Adds 235 Flock Cameras Specifically For Players To Destroy - Kotaku
content:
While GTA VI is still a few short months away, the modders of GTA V are still hard at work, especially WTTDOTM who just released a mod that adds a bunch of Flock cameras to Los Santos. According to a video showing off the mod (via FRVR), the cameras work exactly as they do in real life. “As players drive through the map, they are subjected to seemingly inescapable surveillance, with pictures taken of them every time they enter a new camera’s field of view,” the description reads. “Representing Flock’s own history of inaccurate reporting, every time a player passes through a camera’s field of view, the mod creates a 1 in 20 chance that the [camera] will trigger a police chase without any cause.” But WTTDOTM didn’t create the Grand Theft Automated License Plate Reader mod to add yet another layer of grim verisimilitude; he wants players to destroy the little bastards. The video showcasing the mod is just a montage of the cameras being smashed to bits with cars, rocket launchers, tanks, and more. The destruction is gamified as players can use the cameras to capture stunts and can pick up the components of destroyed cameras for some quick cash, and the mod has a speedrun mode that keeps track of how fast you can tear the cameras down. The mod adds 235 cameras scattered all over the city. In a TikTok video talking about the mod, WTTDOTM said, “Flock is a scourge on America…If you think the 235 in this mod are bad, just understand that that is one-tenth of the cameras currently installed in LA County, which Los Santos is based on.” Don’t miss the latest reviews, news and tips. title: Storylines | RSL v NYC: Fighting for Final Third Rise Above Playoff Line - Real Salt Lake
content: Real Salt Lake return to America First Field this weekend to host New York City FC with a chance to snap the longest winless run of the five-year Pablo Mastroeni era and climb back above the playoff line in the West. NYCFC is simultaneously looking to snap its six-game run without a win, as it holds onto the ninth and final play-in spot in the East. This edition of Storylines looks at the returning players for RSL and takes a deeper look into RSL’s strong home form of 2026, despite recent struggles. RSL FW Sergi Solans returns to availability this weekend after missing the midweek Houston trip, out with an illness during Wednesday’s match against the Dynamo. The Spanish-born rookie forward currently leads the Club’s 2026 Golden Boot race with 13 goals across all competitions, including a new RSL rookie record with nine in MLS action, opening his account on March 7 in RSL’s 3-2 victory over Atlanta (incidentally RSL’s last road victory). Solans’ four-game scoring streak last month started with the 4-0 Leagues Cup victory against Atlante CF. The rookie striker has made the starting spot his own through his dynamic playstyle and finishing ability. During a month that saw him scored in five of six games, ultimately earning a new contract extension, he showcased what made him a first-round pick in the 2025 MLS SuperDraft. Although Solans has now gone three games without scoring against Leon, Colorado and LAFC, his gravity and positioning continues to create multiple opportunities inside the opposition’s penalty area for both himself and his teammates. Former Real Salt Lake academy player Taylor Booth is expected to be available off the RSL bench for the first time since returning to Utah last week. The Utah native, surely excited to be back home and play in front of the home crowd, returns to the Wasatch Front for the first time since the two-time USMNT and Olympic attacker joined Bayern Munich’s academy in 2019. Spending several seasons in the Netherlands with FC Utrecht, where he scored his first professional hat trick on February 4, 2024, against FC Volendam, Booth will soon be reunited on the field with his younger brother, Zach Booth, who arrived back at RSL in January, and suffered a hamstring injury in mid-August. This weekend’s match against New York City FC could also mark the long-awaited return of former RSL captain and USMNT January 2024 midfielder Emeka Eneli, who has been out with a knee injury since January, potentially dressing and being added to the bench for the first time since recovering from his surgery. Real Salt Lake returned from the World Cup break with an impressive 4-1 friendly victory over Burnley FC. A brilliant League Cup group-stage performance saw RSL finish with seven points and advance to the knockout stage. Despite the success against non-MLS teams, RSL have struggled in MLS regular-season play, with injuries and a constantly-changing lineup contributing to the issue. In the recent match at Houston, Real Salt Lake saw a season-high 13 players featured on the availability report, yet still managed to keep itself in the game through gritty defensive play and unproven depth. Unfortunately, the Claret-and-Cobalt conceded yet another late goal, dropping points and extending its winless streak to 10 games, the fourth-longest drought in the Club’s 22-year history. The current run marks the longest RSL winless streak since a 12-game winless streak that spanned from September 7, 2016 until April 1, 2017. Despite the recent struggles, RSL are 7-2-2 (W-L-T) at home in MLS action and 10-2-3 (W-L-T) across all competitions this season at home, recently picking up an important point against LAFC in last Saturday’s outing at America First Field. Real Salt Lake now looks to continue its strong home form against a struggling NYCFC team. The Eastern Conference side arrives in Utah winless in six matches, posting an 0-3-3 (W-L-T) record in MLS play since being eliminated from Leagues Cup. The Pigeons recently lost 2-1 after conceding a 93rd-minute winner to the New England Revolution at Citi Field on Wednesday, adding to their inconsistency this season, struggling to keep themselves in a playoff spot. Real Salt Lake have faced off against New York City FC seven times in the past, holding a record of 4-2-1 (W-L-T). The first meeting came back in 2015, when RSL picked up three points with a 2-0 victory over the New York team. The Claret-and-Cobalt then won the next two matches, scoring a total of 10 goals across the first three meetings. This Saturday’s match will mark the fifth time New York have visited Utah, with RSL previously undefeated against the East Coast team. The Wasatch side has outscored New York 7-2 on aggregate, going 3-0-1 (W-L-T) across those four matches. The clash between the two playoff hopefuls will take place at America First Field on Saturday in what is expected to be RSL’s 16th consecutive sellout, complete with the halftime “Teddy Bear Toss” as the Club’s annual “Kick Childhood Cancer” tradition continues, with kickoff scheduled at 7:30 p.m. MT. Tickets are available at www.rsl.com/tickets/. Bring a new stuffed animal to throw on the field at halftime to donate to kids in need. title: Reges v. Cauce (U.S. 9th Circuit Court, 2025) - Free Speech Center
content: Home » Articles » Case » Academic Freedom » Reges v. Cauce (U.S. 9th Circuit Court, 2025) Stuart Regis, a professor at the University of Washington who was punished for a syllabus statement that interfered with the university's DEI policy, won a free speech lawsuit against the university. (Courtesy of FIRE/Twinkle Don't Blink) This case involves a judgment in favor of Stuart Reges, a computer science professor at the University of Washington, that stressed the importance of academic freedom. Reges had been investigated, reprimanded and threatened with further discipline by university officials after he posted a statement on his course syllabus. It had mocked the university’s model statement intended to acknowledge the university’s proposed land acknowledgment that its campus in Seattle was originally home to indigenous people who owned the land. Instead, he posted a statement saying that “I acknowledge that by the labor theory of property the Coast Saish people can claim historical ownership of almost none of the land currently occupied by the University of Washington.” Claiming that this statement had triggered negative student responses and created a “toxic environment” in his class and interfered with the university diversity, equity and inclusion policies, administrators apologized for his statement, created an alternate section in which his students could enroll and generally subjected him to censorship. He, in turn, filed a claim against university president Magdalena Balazinska and other school officials for “First Amendment retaliation and viewpoint discrimination,” and claimed that the policies he had violated has been “facially overbroad and unconstitutionally vague.” Citing Pickering v. Board of Education (1968), a district court decided that while Reges had spoken on a matter of public concern, the university’s interest “in mitigating disruption to university staff functions, teaching assistants and the learning environment outweighed Reges’ First Amendment interests.” It also dismissed his overbreadth and vagueness claims. The circuit court’s opinion, which reversed the lower court, was written by Daniel Aaron Bress, who was appointed by President Donald Trump in 2019. “The public university occupies a central place in the law of the First Amendment. The First Amendment protects the free exchange of ideas,” Bress wrote. Citing Keyishian v. Board of Regents (1967), he noted that “the classroom is peculiarly the ‘marketplace of ideas,’” and that such freedom is “not without some costs,” including unwanted disruption. Affirming that Reges had engaged in protected speech, that the university had penalized him, and that it did so as a result of his speech, the court found that Reges’ speech interests outweighed the University of Washington’s interest in the case. The court rejected the idea that Reges had engaged in “government speech,” which the University of Washington had the right to control. It noted that the decision in Garcetti v. Ceballos (2006), which had articulated the government speech doctrine, did not decide the issue of “speech related to scholarship or teaching.” In expressing his opinion, Reges had stimulated campus debate, had done so on the very document (a syllabus) that the university had sought to influence, and had spoken in first person (“I”) rather than on behalf of the university. Moreover, as a college professor, he had greater freedom than teachers in primary and secondary schools, which had been the subjects of other suits. The court observed that Reges was speaking not about a private matter but about a matter of public concern, which it characterized as “core political speech.” It further noted that “the parodic manner of Reges’s speech does not detract from its First Amendment value.” The Court further questioned the university’s belief that Reges’ speech had led to inordinate disruption. It noted that “student discomfort and anger” over the speech was an insufficient reason to censure it and that to give it inordinate weight would be to give in to a “heckler’s veto.” It also suggested that the university had presented inadequate proof that Reges’ comment had resulted in difficulties of recruiting or in student flight, questioned whether one student that it claimed had left the university even existed, and suggested that there may have been other reasons that some students left Reges’ class for a section taught by another professor. The court further agreed that the nondiscrimination and affirmative action policies that had justified university action were in fact overbroad and vague. Justice Sidney R. Thomas, a Clinton appointee, wrote a dissenting opinion in which he agreed that the court should apply Pickering balancing but arguing that such balancing worked in favor of the university. He put particular emphasis on the university’s mission to educate Native American students and on the fact that Reges had alternatives other than his syllabus, for which the university had not punished him, to express his opinions. He also thought that the district court’s construction of university policy to save it from overbreadth and vagueness was reasonable and had been warranted. Ultimately, the university awarded Reges $600,000 in damages, sending the signal that the court took the case and the principle of academic freedom seriously. John R. content: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations, or ASEAN, was established on 8 August 1967 in Bangkok, Thailand, with the signing of the ASEAN Declaration (Bangkok Declaration) by the Founding Fathers of ASEAN: Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore and Thailand. Brunei Darussalam joined ASEAN on 7 January 1984, followed by Viet Nam on 28 July 1995, Lao PDR and Myanmar on 23 July 1997, Cambodia on 30 April 1999, and Timor-Leste on 26 October 2025 making up what is today the eleven Member States of ASEAN. ASEAN organs always strive to achieve ASEAN’s goals and objectives, the Secretary-General of ASEAN and the ASEAN Secretariat shall be functioned as coordinating Secretariat to help facilitate effective decision-making withing and amongst ASEAN bodies. In addition, each Member State shall appoint a Permanent Representative to liaise with Secretary-General of ASEAN and the ASEAN Secretariat ASEAN shall develop friendly relations and mutually beneficial dialogues, cooperation and partnerships with countries and sub-regional, regional and international organisations and institutions. This includes external partners, ASEAN entities, human rights bodies, non-ASEAN Member States Ambassadors to ASEAN, ASEAN committees in third countries and international organisations, as well as international / regional organisations. The rodmap for an ASEAN Community (2009-2015) was declared by the leaders in 2009. The ASEAN Community, anchored on three community pillars: Political-Security Community, Economic Community, Socio-Cultural Community was launched in 2015. The ASEAN 2025: Forging Ahead Together was introduced in 2015 as a Post-2015 Vision. The meeting brought together IAI Task Force Members from all ASEAN Member States, representatives from ASEAN Partners and International Organisations, IAI National Coordinators and Focal Points, and officials from the ASEAN Secretariat, providing a key platform to exchange views on the implementation status of the new IAI Work Plan V (2026–2030). Both sides further reiterated their shared commitment to deepening multi-stakeholder collaboration, ensuring effective project delivery, and mobilising resources for the full implementation of the new IAI Work Plan V (2026–2030). title: Liverpool v Fulham: Team news - Liverpool FC
content:
Liverpool are monitoring the fitness of Cody Gakpo ahead of Saturday's visit of Fulham in the Premier League. The attacker was absent on Wednesday night against Atletico Madrid at Anfield with what head coach Andoni Iraola described as 'adductor issues'. Gakpo's status for the clash with Alvaro Arbeloa's side remains doubtful, though Bradley Barcola, who was an enforced substitution in midweek during the second half of his full debut, is set to be available. "We still need to train [on Friday]," Iraola told his pre-match press conference. "We train this afternoon, evening. But, yes, Barcola was just cramps. "Obviously he finished tight in the game and then we have to evaluate with how are things today – but there's no injury. He should be available if everything goes normal. "[With] Cody, we will see. He didn't train yesterday. Today, we will try with him and let's see if he's ready for tomorrow or we need to wait for the next one." You have to accept cookies in order to view this content on our site. Joe Gomez may be available as he closes in on a return from a muscle issue picked up in pre-season, while Federico Chiesa continues his own recovery from injury. Long-term absentees Conor Bradley, Hugo Ekitike and Giovanni Leoni remain sidelined. Iraola provided an update on Ekitike's recovery from a ruptured Achilles tendon. "I think it's difficult with these long-term injuries, I think he's still far [away]," he said. "But we had a meeting with the medical department to analyse when we completed the [squad] list for the European games. There is a reasonable chance that he could help us in the last two games of the group stages. "But it's still very early to say. It's very early because it's a long-term injury [and] a big part of the rehab [he] is still to meet. But if we decide to put him there, it is because there is a hope and there is a realistic chance that he could help us in January." Tom Cairney, with a knee injury, is set to be Fulham's only absentee for the trip to Merseyside. "We have to wait until the last training session," head coach Arbeloa said. "But just Tom [is currently out injured] and we will see after the training session if everyone is ready." Arbeloa, who made 98 appearances for Liverpool between 2007 and 2009, is still searching for his first Premier League points in charge of the Cottagers. On returning to Anfield, the Spaniard said: "It will be so special. I went back when I was a Real Madrid player but now it's my first time as a coach. Anfield will always be a special place for me. "We have a massive game for us and we have been working really hard this week. We know that we have to improve and we need to adjust some parts of our game." title: PRO PALAZZOLO v MILAN FUTURO: MATCH PREVIEW - AC Milan | Sito Ufficiale

title: The candy business or football? Crookston's George Widman V chooses Fighting Hawks - grandforksherald.com
content:
GRAND FORKS — In northeast North Dakota and northwest Minnesota, the name Widman is widely known for iconic candy stores. In 1911, George Widman I opened the Widman's Candy store in Crookston. In 1949, George Widman II started Widman's Candy in Grand Forks. George Widman III and George Widman IV currently own the candy shop in Crookston. As for George Widman V? He's currently trading in the candy business for a clipboard and whistle at UND's Memorial Village. Widman is a 21-year-old UND student in charge of the Fighting Hawks football program's scout team and overseeing the team's equipment staff. "He grew up with a great family," UND head football coach Eric Schmidt said. "Everyone knows the Widman name in the candy business, but he's going to be an excellent football coach. There's no job too small for him, like he's not above anything. He digs in and goes to work, and he'll do it with a lot of quality." Who: No. 6 UND at Portland StateWhen: 9 p.m., SaturdayWhere: Hillsboro, Ore., Hillsboro StadiumStreaming: ESPN+ Three weeks after graduating from Crookston High School in 2023, Widman joined the UND football program. His first tasks were with the equipment staff, then worked into a student assistant role on the defense — working with former UND defensive coordinator Joel Schwenzfeier and veteran UND corners coach Travis Stepps. When Widman first started at UND, he saw former Hawks student assistant Joe Seymour working with the scout team and wanted to have that role. Seymour, who spent six years at UND, is in his second season on the Northwestern staff as a special teams assistant after a short stop at Indiana State. When Schmidt arrived in Grand Forks ahead of last season, Widman transitioned to being Schmidt's assistant and running the scout team. "Last year, he started in defensive (quality control) and by the end of the year was running the scout team and team meetings," Schmidt said. "He had a hand in equipment. Every coach on our defensive side of the ball was using him because of the quality of work. I probably did a poor job managing his workload. It's a testament to young coaches who come in and do a great job and increase value. He'll have the opportunity to be full-time when he graduates." Prior to this season, Widman was planning to help coach at Crookston High School before an opportunity arose and Schmidt called Widman. "I had a great connection with Coach Schmidt," Widman said. "I'd still talk to him like every other week when I was gone. I was juiced up (when he offered a position). How can you pass the opportunity to work with that guy? I mean, he's my role model. My mentor. He's my guy. I look up to him." Schmidt has never hesitated to give Widman additional duties. As UND heads to its first road trip of the 2026 season this weekend in Portland, Widman will be overseeing the equipment operation and travel logistics. "Never in this line of work have I not considered someone because of age," Schmidt said. "If someone is young and energetic and starving to get a foot in the door ... and players love him. He's getting them juiced up every day. There's a really genuine love for what he's doing and everyone appreciates that." As for the candy business, Widman thinks he's found his profession on the football field. "I love doing football every day," Widman said. "I love the guys I work with. They're my guys. title: GTA V modder adds 235 working Flock Cameras to Los Santos, allowing players to destroy “a scourge on America” - FRVR
content: As real-life America gets bombarded with Orwellian security systems in the form of Flock, one GTA V modder has decided to add the oppressive tech into the streets of Los Santos. Hilariously dubbed Grand Theft Automated License Plate Reader, modder WTTDOTM has introduced 235 working Flock Cameras to the streets of Los Santos. As you move around the open-world, these cameras will track your every move, take pictures of you, and do everything Flock Cameras are designed to do. That’s right: as you commit crimes, such as speeding or splattering a line of pedestrians, these cameras will report your actions to the police and continue tracking you across the open-world. Additionally, the cameras can also falsely report you, although not as often as the 70% false reports that their real-world equivalents try to hide. “If you think the 235 in this mod are bad, just understand that that is one-tenth of the cameras currently installed in LA County.” Furthermore, as this is the world of Grand Theft Auto, you can also De-Flock Los Santos. With the power of a well-placed rocket launcher, you can blow up the pesky Big Brother devices and clear a section of the map. If you’re dedicated enough, you can remove all 235 of them, and go back to the good, old-fashioned way of magical police detection. As the virtual Flock Cameras take pictures of you throughout your GTA V adventure, you can save those pictures in widescreen or portrait formats. Additionally, the mod also allows you to place your own cameras across the map to set up your own surveillance state and take screenshots of your best stunts. In a TikTok video advertising the new GTA V mod, the modder explained that the 235 virtual Flock Cameras are already oppressive, but they pale in comparison to the number of cameras installed in American cities. “Flock is a scourge on America,” they said. “It’s a private, eight-billion-dollar surveillance company that operates over 100,000 across the country. If you think the 235 in this mod are bad, just understand that that is one-tenth of the cameras currently installed in LA County, which Los Santos is based on.” While Los Santos isn’t a 1:1 scale version of LA County, there are multiple camera placements which are identical to their real-life counterparts in this mod. While other cameras are close approximations, it still shows how invasive these security cameras are with some looking over public beaches, capturing images of everyone in beachwear and storing them on private company servers. (Let us not forget that Flock Cameras have been used in real life to stalk people.) If you want to bring the surveillance state into your version of Los Santos, you can download the brilliant mod right here. Additionally, the modder is allowing users to submit their own photos taken from the virtual cameras in a fun community challenge. title: Colts' offense thrives in previous matchup v. now-Ravens' coach - Yahoo Sports
content: The Shane Steichen and Daniel Jones-led Indianapolis Colts offense found quite a bit of success last season against Jessie Minter's defense last season when he was the LA Chargers' defensive coordinator. Minter, of course, is now the head coach of the Baltimore Ravens, who face the Colts at home this Sunday to open the regular season. When the Colts and Chargers met last season, the Indianapolis offense was rolling. In this game specifically, the Colts would drop 38 points on Minter's LA defense. Jones was 23-of-34 passing for 288 yards with two scores. Jonathan Taylor rushed for 94 yards on just 16 carries, while Alec Pierce totaled 98 receiving yards on five receptions. As a unit, the Colts were efficient on third down, effective in the red zone, and averaged an impressive 6.9 yards per play. Now, to state the obvious, what happened last year has no bearing on this year's Week 1 matchup. Minter also has different personnel to work with in Baltimore, which can alter what his defensive scheme looks like. That said, Steichen was prepared and capitalized on just about anything the Minter defense threw at the Colts. title: Springboks v All Blacks a US World Cup preview in Baltimore as thrilling series goes down to the wire - The Guardian
content: ‘Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry’ will culminate on US soil on Saturday, a staging post on the road to America hosting the World Cup in 2031 When New Zealand and South Africa kick off at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore on Saturday, there will be more at stake than victory in “Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry”, the four-Test series the Springboks lead 2-1. For World Rugby CEO Alan Gilpin, the game is a key staging post on the road to the 2031 World Cup, which the US will host – a journey that could include Six Nations games on American soil. “We’ve been in a long process with venues and cities, over the last two years,” Gilpin said, of the build to World Cup kick-off. “We’ve still got 25-plus cities involved in that process, which is fantastic in terms of engagement and enthusiasm. “We’ve now done all the basic feasibility, on, ‘Can we play World Cup-standard rugby in these venues, natural turf,’ all the things we’ve got to take into consideration. Now we’re starting to get submissions from the venue, the city, the state sports commission, on what are some of the commercials, economics, provision of services, city by city, venue by venue. And then you overlay tournament window considerations, availability, NFL, MLS and other considerations, and then weather, team movement.” In Baltimore, the weather will be hot and sticky, thunderstorms a chance. For the All Blacks and Springboks, team movement meant a shared flight soon after last Saturday’s game in Soweto, won 29-24 by the Boks. The joint journey was unusual but the world is these days. It’s the first weekend of the NFL season. That may seem like commercial suicide for Gilpin but he noted an irony: as World Rugby makes its big play in Baltimore (with the Ravens in Indianapolis to face the Colts), the NFL is in rugby territory, Australia, for San Francisco 49ers v Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Such is globalization. “Our ambition is to get to Rugby World Cup in Australia [next year] and be able to say these are the smaller number of venues that will host matches in 2031,” Gilpin said. “There’s a lot of different moving parts. … We had matches this year in a number of small venues, for USA Rugby. There’s some learnings you take from that, but there’s nothing like using the sort of venues that we could use for a World Cup.” Baltimore seems well set. The field is grass so there’s no need to drop in a pitch, a process at some stadiums used by the soccer World Cup that prompts thoughts of scrums sliding about on pallets but which Gilpin said research showed would work for rugby. Charm City is close to New York, Philadelphia and Washington DC, American rugby towns also full of general sports fans and easily reached from Europe. On that score, depressingly, World Rugby has had to consider possible problems for fans flying in. Put simply, the present US administration doesn’t like foreigners much. Then again, one group Donald Trump does like is white South Africans, “refugees” admitted in thousands. A thought: show Stephen Miller, Trump’s immigration Nosferatu, how the Springbok pack destroyed the All Blacks in Soweto, and you’ll have rugby content pinged out to Maga faster than ICE can swarm a blue city. Then again, best not tell Trump and his “communist”-hating pals South Africa’s pack is led by a terrifying hooker named Marx. So much for lefty facetiousness. World Rugby focuses on sport. A sell-out of 71,000 will be a record for rugby in the US. How many fans are from the US game, proudly wearing colors of high school, college or club, will be key to see. The stadium announcer will be Matt McCarthy of RugbyWrapUp, a legend of the game in New York. TV-wise, the game will be “on Paramount Plus with CBS Sports Network doing some highlights,” Gilpin said. “We’ve got to work with them over the next two years on getting all that content in place.” Next year is a World Cup year. That usually truncates international schedules but Gilpin said big games would be back in America: “There’s going to be a full Rugby Championship played in a Rugby World Cup year for the first time, which is really interesting because we’re a bit later with our start date in Australia, 1 October … so that’s presenting some opportunities for potential conversation. We definitely will have some marquee matches. That’s hopefully some news we’ll be able to share in the not too distant future.” He subsequently shared news with the British press, saying the Six Nations could come into the mix. “This isn’t a live discussion of an Italy v Ireland game, but why don’t we use that as an example?” Gilpin told the Daily Telegraph. “You’ve got two fantastic fanbases in the US of Irish and Italian fans. If you could take a Six Nations game to the right place, to Boston or to New York … you can definitely drive the economics. Now, you’re going to have Irish fans and Italian fans in those respective home countries saying, ‘Hang on a minute, you know, we want to see our country play?’ The counter-argument to that [is] it’s still Irish and Italian fans getting the chance to watch their team, so they’re just not the ones who live in Ireland and Italy on this occasion. But that’s a balancing piece we’ve got to work through.” Speaking to the Guardian, Gilpin promised “learnings” from the last big US game featuring Ireland, the All Blacks’ win at Soldier Field in Chicago last November which featured technical snafus around a dubious red card. “We’re more directly involved with the two unions and with the match promoter in the way sports presentation looks,” Gilpin said. “How do you make sure the audience is engaged in the right way with big screens and match-day activity? So we’re dialing that up. It’s a learning curve the whole time.” The latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewed In terms of what there is to be learned about the state of the American game, Gilpin like many is concerned about Major League Rugby, the US men’s league now down to just five teams. Latest to leave was Anthem Rugby Carolina, which World Rugby and USA Rugby funded for three years to grow domestic talent. The governing body trumpets a $200m investment for 2031 and the women’s World Cup two years later. Money spent on bringing in the All Blacks and Springboks is part of that total but so is grassroots work. “In all the work we’re doing with USA Rugby, there’s obviously the community and college and club and youth and high school pieces,” Gilpin said. “But on the high-performance national programs … look at the last six months.” Both Eagles sevens teams are doing well and the men’s 15s have won four games on the trot, three in the Nations Cup, a World Rugby event. On Saturday in Osaka, in the Pacific Nations Cup, the Eagles face Japan. About the demise of Anthem, Gilpin stayed off record. Sources say a potential sixth team is in the MLR mix but there isn’t much likelihood of the Anthem experiment being repeated, even in light of successful sub-national World Rugby projects such as the Fijian Drua. Of MLR, Gilpin said there were “continuous conversations. There’s no doubt that the improving performance of the Eagles must be helpful to those conversations.” Back to Baltimore. The first three All Blacks-Springboks Tests were brutal thrillers. Now the All Blacks, without injured men like great No 8 Ardie Savea, must find salvation. In the city of Stringer Bell, Jimmy McNulty and other hard-boiled heroes, World Rugby will hope for a finale that goes down to the wire. Martin Pengelly writes on rugby in the US on Substack, at The National Maul.

title: Influential Atlanta nightclub owner James ‘Mr. V’ Virgil dies at 85 - Atlanta News First
content: ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) — Atlanta nightlife entrepreneur James “Mr. V” Virgil has died at the age of 85. Virgil was born in Mississippi and moved to Chicago before landing in Atlanta. He opened Mr. V’s Figure 8 in 1978 and became a fixture in Atlanta’s nightclub scene. The club’s influence expanded beyond Atlanta thanks to commercials that aired on TBS during the club’s run in the 1980s. After leaving the nightclub business, Virgil pivoted and opened Mr. V’s Restaurant Supplies, which he ran until his death. Atlanta City Councilmember Michael Julian Bond called Virgil “the godfather of Atlanta nightlife.” “I will remember a good natured, generous spirit and a man happy to freely share his wisdom with anyone who sought his guidance,” Bond said. A candlelight vigil is set to be held Tuesday, Sept. 15, at 3131 Campbellton Road SW, near the old entrance to Mr. V’s Figure 8.

title: Kathleen V. Jameson Named Speed Museum Director - Hyperallergic
content: The New Museum’s new board members, Alison Rossiter works acquired by The Met, a record-breaking David Hockney show, and more in Art Movements. Art Movements, published every Thursday afternoon, is a roundup of must-know news, appointments, awards, and other art-world happenings. Kathleen V. Jameson is returning to the Speed Museum, where she spent a formative period of her career, as its new director. A scholar of American art and photography, Jameson comes to the Kentucky institution from the Mint Museum in Charlotte, North Carolina, where she established the first digital media program. Her three-decade trajectory is stacked with roles at the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston; the James A. title: The Mercedes-AMG CLE 646 Spezialanfertigung Heralds a Return to V-8-Powered Sports Coupes - Car and Driver
content: Only 30 units of the CLE 646 Spezialanfertigung, which features extreme aerodynamics and is rear-wheel drive, will be built. Back in January, Mercedes-AMG teased a new high-performance version of the CLE-class coupe, the second car in the brand’s limited-production Mythos series. Now the track-ready beast has been revealed in full, and the Mercedes‑AMG CLE 646 Spezialanfertigung looks just as mean as we expected. Spezialanfertigung roughly translates to “custom-made” in English, and the CLE 646 will be extremely rare, with only 30 units set to be produced. Unsurprisingly, every single one has already been spoken for. The road-legal CLE 646 is based on the AMG CLE53, but has undergone drastic changes. The big news lies under the hood, where Mercedes stuffed a twin-turbo V-8 engine producing 637 horsepower (or 646 PS, hence the name). The 4.0-liter engine also churns out 627 pound-feet of torque, and it features a flat-plane crankshaft design to minimize rotating mass and improve throttle response. The engine employs three separate cooling circuits to stay in its ideal operating window. There is a high-temperature circuit for the engine and two low-temperature circuits focused on charge air heading into the turbos, the transmission oil, and the 48-volt electrical system. The V-8 engine emits a roar through a unique exhaust system developed with help from Akrapovič that uses titanium to shed weight. The CLE 646’s muscle is sent directly to the rear wheels, one of the most significant changes versus the CLE53 upon which it is based. Instead of all-wheel drive, power is routed to the rear wheels through a nine-speed automatic transmission and an electronically controlled limited-slip rear differential. Mercedes-AMG says the CLE 646 will rocket its way to 62 mph in 3.9 seconds. 124 mph arrives in a claimed 11.4 seconds, and the top speed is listed at 193 mph. When it comes to handling, the CLE 646 is fitted with a specially developed steel sprung coilover suspension with four-way adjustable dampers, which have low-speed and high-speed rebound and compression settings that can be set independently. To slow down, the car uses ventilated and perforated carbon-ceramic brake discs measuring 16.5 inches up front and 14.2 inches at the rear. The front discs are clamped by six-piston fixed calipers, while the rear axle features single-piston floating calipers. The styling is just as wild as the powertrain, with an aggressive stance provided by a body that measures 2.4 inches wider and features additional reinforcements to maximize stiffness. Those bulging front fenders, which have huge air outlets carved into them, are fashioned from carbon fiber, as is the rest of the front end, side sills, hood, roof, and rear bumper. Mercedes claims that the CLE 646 weighs around 375 pounds less than a CLE53, helped by other changes such as a polycarbonate rear window and rear side windows and a lighter 12-volt starter battery. The front end is covered in intakes, and along with looking badass, they also help cool the engine and brakes. The grille now extends all the way to the front splitter, and is joined by a sizable hood vent. At the rear, there’s a ginormous diffuser, stacked quad exhaust outlets, and, of course, an unmissable rear wing with a manually adjustable center section. Mercedes says the extreme aerodynamics produce over 550 pounds of downforce at top speed. The CLE 646 also rides on 20-inch forged wheels, with 305/30 front tires and 335/30 rear tires. The interior takes an equally extreme approach, ditching the rear seats and acoustic insulation material and sporting a simpler sound system. There are also fewer drive modes and assistance systems, cutting the number of controls on the steering wheel, and the CLE 646 is fitted with racing bucket seats. There’s an optional Performance package that brings six-point harnesses, and the door panels are also now made from carbon fiber. The CLE 646 Spezialanfertigung follows Mercedes-Benz’s first Mythos car, the Mercedes-AMG PureSpeed, a wild roadster based on the SL63 but missing a roof or windshield. There’s no word on how much the CLE 646 Spezialanfertigung costs, but given its limited production run, we have to imagine it’s quite a bit more than the CLE53’s $78,850 starting price. Caleb Miller began blogging about cars at 13 years old, and he realized his dream of writing for a car magazine after graduating from Carnegie Mellon University and joining the Car and Driver team. He loves quirky and obscure autos, aiming to one day own something bizarre like a Nissan S-Cargo, and is an avid motorsports fan. We may earn a commission for purchases made through our links.

title: Storylines | Utah Royals v. Houston Dash: A Chance to Spark a Late Season Surge - Real Salt Lake
content: All eyes shift to the Lone Star State this weekend as the Utah Royals face the Houston Dash on Saturday evening. With the recent rollercoaster of wins and losses for the Utah side, URFC’s history against the Dash poises Head Coach Jimmy Coenraets’ squad with the ability to regain momentum heading into its final stretch of matches. In this edition of storylines we’ll take a closer look at one Utah Royal who continues to be a key producer for URFC’s power offense and could shatter an NWSL record this weekend, the exciting new addition to the Royals and the club's history with the Houston Dash. The Utah Royals head into the weekend road match caught in a win-loss cycle, alternating results in each of its last eight matches. While Coenraets’ squad has continued to find the back of the net, scoring 18 goals in its last eight matches, the squad has only come away with four victories in the span. With seven games remaining in the NWSL regular season, URFC will look to recreate the form that earned it a 10 game unbeaten streak at the beginning of the season and finish on a high before what many hope is the club’s first-ever appearance in the post season. While the Utah side is looking to break another record and earn its first-ever playoff berth, one instrumental piece to the URFC attack can break an NWSL single season record on Saturday evening. Canadian forward Cloé Lacasse has enjoyed a red-hot 2026 season, netting seven goals and recently earning her 10th assist to now sit in a three way tie with Tobin Heath (Portland 2016) and Croix Bethune (Washington 2024). With the Kansas City Current playing Friday evening, there is a chance for the record to change before the Royals kickoff Saturday. Bethune, who also currently has 10 assists, can move into sole possession of a NWSL single-season record 11, while another Lacasse assist against Houston would once again bring the two level at the top. The veteran forward has been instrumental in Utah’s historic 2026 campaign, emerging as one of the driving forces behind the Royals’ newfound identity as a top attacking threat. Lacasse brings speed and an ability to cut through defenders with the ball at her feet to consistently create space for her and her teammates, while her creativity in the final third has added another dimension to the Utah attack. Whether it’s creating chances herself or finding the final pass, Lacasse has become a vital piece of Coenraets’ attack and the forward is a major reason for the Royals 2026 success. Along with the Canadian veteran comes a new addition to the Royals front line, forward Jameese Joseph who joined URFC last week from the Chicago Stars. Since joining the NWSL in 2024, the forward has netted eight goals (including playoffs) and four assists in her young professional career. The 24-year-old Maryland native has proven to beat defenders with both the ball at her feet and by making creative runs in the attacking third. Joseph is a highly versatile forward whose explosive speed and dynamic abilities on and off the ball will be a boost to the URFC attack. With the Royals current attacking threats like Lacasse and the new addition of Joseph, the Utah side has all the tools necessary to right the recent rollercoaster of results and end the season on a run before heading into the postseason. While URFC has found itself unable to consistently earn points since the summer break, this weekend's Lone Star State opponent poses an opportunity for the Royals to regain the momentum that catapulted Utah to the top of the NWSL standings earlier this season. Since the Return of Royalty in 2024, the Utah Royals have historically performed well against the Houston Dash, earning results and boasting an overall record of 3-1-1 (W-L-T) against the club. In the last meeting between the two sides on May 6, Utah earned a 2-0 victory in front of a home crowd at America First Field with Lacasse and Utah native, Courtney Brown netting goals to go along with a stellar performance by the defense and veteran goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn who earned her fourth consecutive clean sheet in the victory. Similarly to the Royals who have been on a rollercoaster of wins and loses as of late, Houston enters the weekend on a three game losing streak. After dominating the Chicago Stars in a 6-0 victory on August 19, the Dash have fallen to Bay, Seattle and Orlando in its most recent three matchups. Although Houston has struggled a bout of losses, its squad features key players like rookie forward Kat Rader who has enjoyed an impressive season thus far. The first year professional sits atop Chicago’s Golden Boot leaderboard with nine goals and one assist, including her first career NWSL brace in the 6-0 victory over Chicago. The former Duke Blue Devil has entered the NWSL in stride, following a prolific collegiate career Rader has continued to showcase her versatility in the attack and lethal scoring ability when she receives the ball in the 18-yard-box. For the Royals to earn a result on Saturday the defense will need to work as a brick wall to stop Rader who finds success with smart movements both on and off the ball. The URFC attack will look to pressure the defense early to get onto the board first and continue its strong 2026 season and historically positive outcomes against the Houston side. The Utah Royals road matchup against the Houston Dash on Saturday, September 12 is scheduled to kickoff at 6:45 p.m. MT and will be streaming on ION. Following this weekend's trip, URFC returns to the Wasatch Front, welcoming former Utah Royal Ally Sentnor and Angel City FC to America First Field on Sunday, September 20. title: ‘X-Men’ Movie: Asa Germann Nabs Role of Angel (Exclusive) - The Hollywood Reporter
content: Subscribe for full access to The Hollywood Reporter Subscribe for full access to The Hollywood Reporter The actor had auditioned to play Cyclops, but will instead be given a chance to grow his wings. The X-Men continued to gather around Professor X. Asa Germann, known for his roles in superhero series Gen V and horror hit Scream 7, is in final talks for a high flying key role in Marvel Studios’ X-Men revival. Much of the cast has already been revealed as Marvel has been meeting and reading and testing actors throughout the summer. The roll call already includes Sadie Sink (Jean Grey), Kit Connor (Cyclops), Christopher Abbott (Prof. X), Samara Weaving (Emma Frost), Inde Navarrette (Rogue) and Maya Boyd (Storm). Adam Driver is also among the cast as the villain Mr. Sinister. Germann was among those who was up for the role of Cyclops. Connor nabbed that role but the Kevin Feige-led studio was impressed enough with Germann that they offered him the part of Warren Worthington III, aka Angel. The character, created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby, was introduced in the very first issue of X-Men back in 1963. Among his attributes are feathered wings on his back, giving him the ability to fly. During one part of his history, Angel was maimed and his wings were replaced by metal projectile-shooting wings by the villain Apocalpyse. The character appeared twice before on the big-screen. Ben Foster played him in 2006’s X-Men: The Last Stand while Ben Hardy played him in 2016’s X-Men: Apocalypse. Fans have felt the character never received a proper movie outting and this could prove to be the opportunity to have him soar into the limelight. Jake Schreier (Thunderbolts) is directing the feature that has a release date of May 5, 2028. Germann already has superhero credentials as he played Samuel “Sam” Riordan in Gen V, the spinoff of The Boys that centered on super-powered young adults attending a crimefighting university. In Scream 7, he played Lucas Bowden, a young man who meets an untimely end on a bar tap ornament. He is repped by CAA, Brillstein Entertainment Partners, and Jackoway Austen. title: Tiafoe v Shelton US Open semi-final a legacy of the departing Gaël Monfils - The Guardian
content: Veteran Frenchman bowed out in New York but the clash of two black players in the last four of the men’s singles is testament to his effect The early days of this year’s US Open can be told in a series of farewells to competitors who plan to end their careers this year. The most moving of them all came in the form of Gaël Monfils’s grand departure inside Louis Armstrong Stadium against the wildly talented 20-year-old Learner Tien. Tien was competing in front of his home crowd, one of the Americans capable of a deep run, but for much of his straight-sets defeat the Frenchman had the American crowd in the palm of his hands. Beyond the massive popularity he has garnered among tennis fans, one of the most striking parts of Monfils’s long farewell was seeing how highly nearly all of his fellow professionals, particularly his fellow black players, regard him. Frances Tiafoe says he spent his youth looking up to Monfils. Arthur Fils considers Monfils his older brother. Naomi Osaka’s nickname for Monfils, one of her idols, is simply “the Goat”. They all hold Monfils in such great esteem, and for good reason. While women’s tennis has witnessed the successes of a long line of top black players, Monfils and his retired compatriot Jo-Wilfried Tsonga were, for so long, the standard bearers for black players in men’s tennis. In the same year that the 40-year-old Monfils will finally bow out, the new generation of black men’s players have consolidated their positions at the top of the sport. Last month, the Cincinnati Open featured two black players competing in a Masters 1000 final for the first time as the 22-year-old Frenchman Fils overcame a year of injuries to defeat Tiafoe and win his first big title. Fils’s victory was preceded by Ben Shelton’s triumph at the Canadian Open in Montreal. It took three weeks for the Fils v Tiafoe final to be eclipsed by an even more significant match between two black players. Tiafoe and Shelton will compete against each other in the US Open semi-finals on Friday night, with the winner becoming the first black man since Jo-Wilfried Tsonga at the 2008 Australian Open, and the first African American man since MaliVai Washington, the 1996 Wimbledon finalist, to reach a grand slam final. The victor will then attempt to become the third black man to win a grand slam after Arthur Ashe and Yannick Noah. Along with last year’s semi-finalist Félix Auger-Aliassime, there will be four black players inside the ATP’s top 11. The status commanded by Monfils, who never reached a major final, plainly underlines how important this moment is for future generations of black tennis players as well as themselves. As Americans at the US Open, two players who have spent their careers being reminded of how far American men’s tennis has fallen since its decades of dominance over the sport, and particularly of Andy Roddick’s triumph at the 2003 US Open, the last time an American man won a title here, the significance of this moment is doubly important to Tiafoe and Shelton. Unlike in their previous runs, there are no multiple grand-slam champions or all-time greats left in the draw, with the earlier semi-final feauturing top seed Alexander Zverev against former top-10 player Karen Khachanov. All four can win this title. The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action The past few years in New York have been leading up to this match. It is just the fourth time Shelton has competed in the US Open main draw, yet somehow this will be his third US Open meeting with Tiafoe. Shelton won their 2023 quarter-final before Tiafoe exacted revenge in a bruising five-set, third-round match in 2024. They have become great friends, which can be awkward oncourt for some, but they enjoy battling against each other so much that their relationship only makes them even more determined to produce their best. It helps they are such creative, all-court players with great variation and explosive athleticism, which makes for such a complementary match-up. This is a third major semi-final for both players, but neither man has ever been so well prepared. Shelton just delivered the biggest win of his career over the defending champion Carlos Alcaraz and the 23-year-old continues to evolve into a genuine grand slam threat. Tiafoe, meanwhile, has been one of the revelations this year. The 28-year old has spent the season determined to be more professional and focused each week than ever before, and his results are a direct consequence of his growing maturity. Their efforts have yielded by far the biggest opportunity of their careers, and the winner will be decided by which competitor is truly ready for the pressure and weight that accompanies such a massive opening.

title: Steichen details challenges Colts face in Week 1 game v. Ravens - Yahoo Sports
content: As Indianapolis Colts' head coach Shane Steichen detailed on Wednesday, the Baltimore Ravens can present significant challenges on both sides of the football. "Got a lot of respect for what they do," Steichen said, via Locked on Colts. "Starts with their quarterback, Lamar, he's a guy that can kind of do everything. He can beat you with your legs, his arm. So we got to jsut do a great job of containing him. The running back Henry is going into Year 11. We need all hands on deck. He's a hell of a runner. We got to rally on the football. Zay Flowers is a good player on the outside; we need to know where he's at. Mark Andrews is a good player. So we're looking forward to that challenge." There is a potential balance that the Colts' pass rush will have to strike when it comes to rushing Jackson. Being overly aggressive can create running lanes for him to escape through, while attempting to keep him in the pocket could provide Jackson with time to survey the field and make plays with his arm. The Colts' linebacker unit will be tested right away in having to help contain Henry, while also attempting to limit Andrews' impact in the passing game. Steichen then continued, "And offensively, looking at it from a defensive perspective, Trey Hendrickson's one of the best in the business rushing the passer. So just containing him as much as we can. Linebacker Smith is a hell of a player. He's been doing it for a long time. Hamilton, safety, nickel, kind of do it all for them. Great player. Humphrey, Wiggins, Starks, all those guys on the back end, but just a lot of respect for their team going into this first matchup." Hendrickson has often lined up on the right side of the defensive line in his career, but we will see if he takes more snaps on the left side to match up with Jalen Travis, who has just four career starts under his belt. The Colts have plenty of playmaking potential at the skill positions, but as Steichen lays out, this is a talented Ravens' defense at the second and third levels. The play of the Colts' offensive line and their ability to create running lanes and keep Daniel Jones clean can be a neutralizer. title: AFL finals: where the Brisbane v Adelaide semi-final will be won and lost | Martin Pegan - The Guardian
content: The Lions are now on the long road to a premiership three-peat as they host the Crows with a preliminary final clash with the Hawks on the line Brisbane had a path laid out for them to book a home preliminary final on the way to a fourth straight grand final when they locked in third spot and set up a qualifying final against an embattled Sydney. But the two-time reigning premiers were blown off course as they were a step off the pace from the early exchanges then outworked by the inspired Swans in a humbling defeat. The Lions walked the same tightrope 12 months ago when they were hammered by the Cats before bouncing back in a semi-final against the rising Suns. Coach Chris Fagan’s side went on to take the long road to success across four finals last year – just as they had done in 2024 – to win a second consecutive premiership. They will now need to do the same again to claim a three-peat. Adelaide put their painful recent history behind them when they shook off a late Western Bulldogs rally to secure their first finals victory in nine years. After snapping their finals hoodoo and at the same time banishing the ghosts of last year’s straight-sets exit as minor premiers, the Crows can now play with the shackles released. The weight of expectation that comes with a home final has been thrown off as Matthew Nicks’ side hit the road to take on the back-to-back reigning premiers while hoping to have two games at the MCG – starting with Hawthorn next week – still to come. History suggests that to write Brisbane off would be at your own peril. But something feels different this time. There were signs of decline against Sydney, or at least fatigue, from a battle-hardened side that has reached the past three deciders and is playing in an eighth-straight finals series. The Lions are leaking heavy scores, including nine triple-figure totals this season and more than 20 goals in three of the past 14 games. The 141 points conceded against the Swans was the most from the Lions in 21 finals under Fagan, though they can point to all 12 of the previous teams to lose a final by 50 points or more this century then bouncing back to win the next week. The Lions’ woes this year have often started with defending their own turnovers and they are ranked in the bottom-four for points conceded from the source. With Lachie Neale – the No 1-ranked centre clearance player in the league – leading the onball brigade, they can usually rely on getting the ball going their way from the middle. But even the star-studded midfield misfired against the Swans as they were outscored 39-6 from centre ball-ups. Will Ashcroft, Hugh McCluggage and Neale were all well below their best and will be eager to respond. Adelaide had to dig deep to clinch a breakthrough finals victory against the Bulldogs and continue what has turned into a promising campaign since their mid-season bye. The Crows have won 10 of 13 matches in the second half of the year including triumphs over top-six sides the Cats and Swans, while losing to the Dockers in their only other clash against one of the remaining teams. Nicks’ side found the genuine contenders harder to handle earlier as they lost games against the Cats, Dockers and Hawks, while copping their heaviest defeat of the year against the Lions. The Crows have had recent troubles against the Lions with only two wins in 10 matches since 2018, and five losses from as many meetings at the Gabba in that time. But this is the first time the two teams have crossed paths in a final for 23 years, and Adelaide now have a defence made for finals as the second-best side for points conceded this year. Turning that reliable defence into regular attack remains a concern with the Crows ranked in the bottom-four for defensive-50 to inside-50 chains – just the weakness in the Lions’ game they should target after the Swans exploited it so well. Jonathan Horn brings expert analysis on the week's biggest AFL stories Lachie Neale: The dual Brownlow medallist put aside personal issues and speculation around his playing future to have another outstanding season – at least until he lowered his colours in Brisbane’s loss to Sydney. Neale was held to only 18 disposals and two clearances – his lowest tally at stoppages over the past year – in the qualifying final and will want to get his clean hands on the ball more to lead the Lions’ response. The former skipper need only look back to the last time the Lions played the Crows for a reminder of the influence he can have, when he ran riot and gathered 42 disposals in a resounding victory in round seven. Neale might be headed for the exit once the Lions’ campaign ends but if he can hit his usual heights over the next three weeks, success is likely to follow and ensure he earns a warm send-off. Izak Rankine: The Adelaide dynamo has hit a rich vein of form as he continues to atone for using a homophobic slur towards an opponent and being banned for last year’s finals series. Rankine has averaged 36 disposals, 10 clearances and two goals across the past four matches while spending more time in the engine room, including in the first final of his career against Western Bulldogs. The 26-year-old was the difference as the Crows held off the Dogs’ final-term charge and capped the stirring victory with the sealer from the tightest of angles. Rankine remains one of the Crows’ main goal threats but as arguably the most in-form and impactful midfielder in the competition he can expect to have the Lions’ Josh Dunkley for company in their semi-final. Brisbane made it difficult to trust them again after such a lacklustre qualifying final performance but have the runs on the board to suggest they will bounce back against an Adelaide side that has too often been exposed for being a rung below the genuine contenders this year.

title: The Supreme Court Ruled in West Virginia v. B.P.J. Now What? - JD Supra
content:
On June 30, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court issued its decision in West Virginia v. B. P. J., 609 U.S. ___, 146 S. Ct. 2356 (2026). The Court held that schools may limit participation in girls’ and women’s sports to cisgender girls and women (women who were assigned female at birth) without violating Title IX[1] or the Equal Protection Clause.[2] The Court determined that limiting women’s teams to cisgender women is substantially related to the government’s interests in safety and competitive fairness. This ruling is narrow in several important ways. It is not a mandate. The ruling addresses whether, under Title IX and the Equal Protection Clause, schools and states may limit women’s sports to cisgender women, not whether they must do so. The ruling is explicitly limited to the sports context. This decision does not address or overturn Grimm v. Gloucester County School Board, 822 F.3d 709 (4th Cir. 2016), the Fourth Circuit case regarding transgender student bathroom access. Indeed, Justice Gorsuch’s concurrence in B.P.J. emphasized that “sex-segregated bathrooms, locker rooms, and dress codes” were not before the Court. Virginia has no laws regarding separating sports by biological sex, and eligibility for athletics is primarily governed by the Virginia High School League (“VHSL”), not individual school boards. Currently, VHSL’s rule limits participation on girls’ sports teams to cisgender girls. Questions about how this ruling applies to your school division’s specific circumstances should be directed to your school division’s legal counsel. [1] Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 is a federal civil rights law that prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex in educational programs and activities that receive federal financial assistance. [2] The Equal Protection Clause is part of the Fourteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution. It, in part, prohibits discrimination by state and local governments.
